title: Isolation Forest
description: Tree-based anomaly detection isolating outliers through partitioning.
name: Isolation Forest
summary: Isolation Forest isolates anomalies by randomly partitioning features. Outliers require fewer splits to isolate in tree hierarchies, resulting in significantly shorter path lengths.
use_when: Detecting tabular outliers or fraud anomalies in high-dimensional datasets without labels.
avoid_when: Dataset consists of dense images or long sequence streams where DL models perform better.
pros: Excellent time complexity scaling, making it highly suitable for massive production data streams.
Natively handles multi-modal distributions without needing distance calculations.
Does not assume any specific probability distribution of the data.
cons: Produces axis-parallel splits which can create artifacts/ghost clusters.
Hyperparameter tuning can be subjective due to lack of labeled validation data.
Suffers from performance degradation if feature spaces are dominated by noise.

key_hyperparams.name: contamination
key_hyperparams.note: The proportion of outliers in the dataset. Crucial for boundary definition.

quick_start:
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
import numpy as np

X = np.array([[-1.1], [0.3], [0.5], [100.0]])
clf = IsolationForest(random_state=0).fit(X)
preds = clf.predict(X)  # -1 for anomaly, 1 for normal
